verdict.tagline: Vast open worlds hide cryptic quests and stubborn technical flaws.
for_you_if: you love deep exploration without hand-holding
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates on release hardware
you dislike relying on external guides for quests
you lack patience for repetitive side dungeons

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: The opening hours offer sparse direction and vast exploration alongside technical crashes and missing graphical options.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening hours as confusing, with little direction given on where to go or what the main goals are.

citations.review_text: I don't even know what i'm doing

I was initially an elden ring hater. I claimed (without actual and objective evidence) that the game was not it. Boy was I wrong. Elden Ring brings together all the components I love about gaming. It brings our beloved souls series character, while providing this immersive and captivating story. But hear me. If you are not into that type of game that just drops into an open world map and gives you suttle hints of what to do, then elden ring might not be it for you. Even then I'd still suggest you try. There's a bit of everything for everyone. Enjoy!

Sometimes makes me want to just die but still great game like it kinda pisses me off that they dont tell you anything but like its ok and also just dont give up and also try not to smash your monitor when playing.
I hated this game at first for being confused but then I understood where to go what to do and I understood what to do and once I beaten my first boss I knew this game was gonna be absolute cinema

this game is peak amazing visuals great boss fights and overall just a peak game to play alone. but the only thing is that it is very confusing at first. i was personally going to return the game at multiple points because i didn't know what to do or where to go but then i learned that that's why the game is so good its your own to figure out, to explore, to discover and overall after you find that out, the game truly becomes peak.

Cant wait to play it some more

I like how it is an open world and that there is so much to explore and uncover.
Hard but rewarding game. Even in the opening area there are so many caves and dungeons filled with secrets and unique items. Combat is well thought out and engaging. Overall 5/5
its my fav open world game it actually is probalbly my favourite game.
The map was full of content. You can explore and be anywhere. Plus its an addiction for solo explorers.

Was looking forward to this and it is probably an amazing game but what is a great game if it performs horribly?

One of the best games ive played not going to lie and runs great just wish they updated some graphical settings by adding dlss or uncapping fps although i understand thats not possible do to how the physics is connected to your fps.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Severe stuttering issues interrupt play while missing quest guidance drives players toward online wikis and optional dungeons feel repetitive.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience severe stuttering and performance issues that make the game unplayable, noting problems with Windows affinity settings and micro stutters that require switching to windowed borderless.

citations.review_text: i have a combined 700 hours in this game across different platforms but i can not in any manner recommend you download this game in the current state regardless of any fix every a short time of playing i experience stuttering that progressively get worse making the game unplayable i loved playing this game now i can't play and not worth the second purchase on pc.

First time playing summer 2026. 

I watched a guide for samurai because I really didn't want to struggle - but then ended up messing up one part so I super struggled first 2 bosses lol but eventually did it. 

It's one of those games where you get no quest guidance what so ever, you got to look up online to follow quests. Also it's really easy to find items you need, you just google it - same with quests.

Just look up a beginner guide for your class it's very helpful for getting started.

I made a second character as a prophet and actually enjoy it more than samurai. I like the versatility of classes and different play styles and there are plenty of guides to help out with really good builds online which makes the game more fun in my opinion - as the bosses get increasingly difficult you need the gear and levels to support that for sure. 

I like that some bosses are fairly easy and then some are super hard. It's a rewarding game for sure. I havn't even completed the game yet - I am taking my time and enjoying the ride. I take breaks from bosses when it feels like I am burning out, switch characters, do some levelling or upgrade gear - explore new places or whatever, there is tonnes to do!

Wasn't a big fan of paying so much on a sale but it is honestly worth it. I wasn't a big fan of dark souls 3 to be honest - but this game is way more enjoyable for me. Graphics look good too, I was getting micro stutters but since switching to windowed borderless it has fixed it. :)
Loved it. My only complaint is the Windows affinity issues making the game essentially unplayable without the mod that allows one to change affinities.

claims.claim: The open world design lacks quest guidance, leading players to rely on online guides and wikis to track quests and find items.

citations.review_text:
Elden Ring is obviously not a bad game. With such an overwhelmingly positive reception, it is clear that it works incredibly well for a lot of people.

But taste is subjective, and after 73 hours and several attempts to get properly into it, I think I can fairly say that this game is not for me.

I enjoyed the Dark Souls games in the past, but at some point I think I grew tired of this style of gameplay. Elden Ring takes that formula and expands it into a huge open world, which is both its greatest strength and one of its biggest weaknesses for me. If you love difficult exploration, environmental storytelling, build experimentation, and discovering things with minimal guidance, this could be an amazing experience. If you enjoy using interactive maps, wikis, and progression guides on a second monitor, it may also fit you well.

For me though, I prefer games where the story, characters, and quests actively pulls me forward. My biggest issue with FromSoftware’s Souls-style games has always been that they do not feel like RPGs in the way I personally enjoy RPGs. There is lore, atmosphere, and worldbuilding, but the storytelling is very indirect and cryptic. If you mainly want a character-driven RPG with story choices and clear quest progression, Elden Ring may disappoint you.

There are absolutely things I like about the game. The atmosphere is excellent, the world feels oppressive, and defeating a difficult boss after learning its patterns can be very satisfying. I also understand why the lack of difficulty settings appeals to many players, because it makes those victories feel more earned.

But many of the same things that make the game rewarding for others make it frustrating for me. The game often feels like it does not respect my time: there is no normal pause function, death can mean losing resources, some runbacks are tedious, and questlines can be so obscure that I often felt pushed toward using a wiki. I do not mind difficulty, but I do mind feeling like I need…

claims.claim: Optional dungeons like catacombs, caves, and mines feature repetitive and copy-and-paste layouts that feel less inspired than the rest of the world.

citations.review_text:
This game was incredibly disappointing to play.
For starters, this game is absolutely beautiful. The set pieces, the enemies, the backgrounds, the game is gorgeous to an unbelievable degree. What I find a bit lacking, however, is that a lot of the enemies and levels can feel overdesigned and clunky to a degree where the deeper thoughts of the design are unreadable. While high gothic architecture is always appreciated, it can definitely feel eye glazing at times when the developers obviously didn't care as much about a location as others. The biggest problems I found with this being the numerous catacombs, caves, forts, and mines that are present throughout the game. Although they are at numerous locations, with very distinct landscapes, there's never anything visually interesting about them that wasn't done before. It makes it feel very video-gamey and copy and paste, when I felt that the worldbuilding of this game was incredibly interesting originally.

The difficulty of the game is far higher than previous souls titles, which in itself is not bad. However, there is a clear distinction between boss encounters. There's Margit, who feel very intentionally designed, while remaining difficult in a fair way, maintaining the "I died, what did I do wrong" mindset that many of the previous games seem to hold. Then there's Knight Ordovis, which is a boss encounter stapling two mini-bosses you have already fought, then taking to precautions to make it feel like a well-made duo boss. The first knight will always cover the second's punish windows, and if you're unlucky, they will attack at such intervals where it is impossible to not take damage. The vast majority of this game is a good boss fight, followed by 2 or 3 boring to bad ones (Some of these being repeat bosses that you have already fought plenty of times before). The difficulty, then, feels less like a natural result of the game attempting to challenge you in an interesting way, but devolves into feeling like it is o…
This is one of the most impressive and expansive games I've played in a long while.  The shear scale of the world and its dungeons is insane.

cohorts.summary: Long term exploration reveals recycled boss encounters and deeply obscure narratives that demand external research.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the open world features reused boss encounters and repetitive smaller dungeons such as caves and catacombs.

citations.review_text:
I love Elden Ring so much, it truly sits at a special place in my heart.
The gameplay, stories it tells, world, music and characters remain as a somber piece of joy for me and I am truly graceious for having been able to experience all of it. Elden Ring is one of my favourite games to pick up and play again. The DLC is very strong and basically just adds onto the already great world.
My main critique is that the game sometimes feels a little *too* big which leads to a lot of bosses being reused, despite this the world still feels very alive and very satisfying to explore. I strongly recommend playing this amazing SoulsBorn experience, it's always a pleasure to return to.

Elden Ring is a fascinating evolution of the Souls formula. I was skeptical about moving the series into a fully open world, but it worked much better than I expected.

The game offers an incredible amount of freedom. You can experiment with countless character builds, approach challenges in different ways, and explore a massive world filled with interesting locations, deep lore, and a huge variety of enemies. Some boss fights are genuinely memorable, although others suffer from extremely delayed animations that can make fights feel less satisfying than they should.

The open world design is both the game's biggest strength and its biggest weakness. Compared to the more focused structure of Dark Souls or Bloodborne, Elden Ring sometimes feels a little too stretched out. Many caves, catacombs, and smaller dungeons start to feel repetitive after a while, with similar layouts and rewards.

The quality of exploration also decreases in later parts of the game. The Mountaintops of the Giants especially show that a bigger world does not always mean a better one, as this area feels much less interesting compared to the earlier regions.

Despite these issues, Elden Ring is still a very enjoyable action RPG with a unique atmosphere, great combat, and a huge amount of freedom. It successfully brings the Souls formula into an open world, even if some parts of the experience feel less polished compared to FromSoftware's more focused games.

Pros:

+ Huge variety of character builds
+ Interesting lore and world building
+ Many memorable enemies and locations
+ Great combat system
+ Lots of exploration

Cons:

- Some bosses rely too much on delayed attacks
- Many caves and catacombs feel too similar
- The open world can feel less focused than previous Souls games
- Later areas are weaker

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the narrative and character motivations as cryptic, obscure, and difficult to comprehend without external guides or item descriptions.

citations.review_text:
I think this is going to be my game for a long long while. I played it for a bit after I got it a couple years ago and then I wasn't able to because of life... I just resumed it and thought "maybe I should just play from the start" but as soon as I loaded my old savefile from a couple years ago I felt so much nostalgia of all I had accomplished so far back then and was able to immerse myself right into it. The combat is so fun and I don't mind getting put in my place for being greedy or on the other hand just doing what some call "cheesing" a boss,  (specially those ones where there is more than lne, you know exactly which ones I mean) if the game has given you tools then you are welcome to use them! Nd besides, you are supposed to play games for fun! If you feel like you shouldn't "cheese" a boss then don't do it because if the healthbar moves then it probably can be killed in some other way.

Talking about that I didn't mind having to find a different weapon at a couple points so far where a boss I was fighting was some sort of resistan to my weapons because there are a LOT of options for weapons of all kinds. 

I think it's interesting how the lore and story is portrayed, while it is a bit cryptic and obscure it's far from bad or unengaging. If you didn't understand a characters motivations or reasons then maybe you skipped the dialog or didn't do a couple seconds or reading.

I have seen some others complain in this manner when faced with the quest to become elden lord "Why should I do that thing" who cares? Not everything needs an explanation. 

This game is a lot of fun. I can't wait to destroy the world or something maybe once I reach the end again and again...

Ps. Blackguard, Mate... Next time I will do it differently and maybe we will still share some boiled crab and prawns after I become Elden Lord.

The first maybe 40 or so hours was some of the most fun I've ever had in any video game, and I realize I've been chasing that high ever since, and somehow it only got worse. 

Firstly, the most blatant weakness for me is the storytelling: it's a joke. I can tell there's some interesting lore and characters somewhere in there, but it's presented in a completely incomprehensible manner. 

"You must seek the Elden Ring and become Elden lord!" okay, cool. Why? You are given the vaguest of the vaguest motivations to do *anything* in this game. I meet random characters with absolutely no context or build-up, that apparently I'm supposed to care for.  I have no idea who am I fighting and why. There's barely any RP in this supposed RPG, as joining 'factions' and completing side-quests is completely inconsequential. Not to mention those aforementioned side-quests have incredibly obscure requirements to complete, some feel almost impossible without the wiki.

I understand FromSoft is known for indirect storytelling, but when you want to tell a classic, multilayered fantasy epic, this style simply does not work. It's a completely ridiculous proposition that I'm supposed to rely on vague item descriptions to understand major plot points. Again, this would be fine on some other game that wasn't heavily touted as "having a great narrative written by George RR Martin!!"

Once I realized the story was pretty much non-existent, my open world immersion and suspension of disbelief was irrecoverably shattered. I began to see cool ruins as nothing more than simple repeated 3D assets thrown randomly across the landscape. It's absolutely clear that the devs had no idea what the story behind most places in this game really was, they just expect the players to fill in the blanks. That is not even mentioning the INSANE amount of recycled areas, enemies and bosses in this game. 

Well, the story is kind of bad, at least the game can redeem itself with its gameplay right? Eh, sort of. Like I s…
